Invoke-WebInventory.ps1 - third-party notices

The script reads the rule packs (1, 2) as data at runtime. Each pack records its upstream commit in its
"source" field and its version suffix (+<commit>). Items 4 and 5 are methods re-implemented in the script's
opt-in probe code (-TlsFingerprint); no upstream code is shipped.

1. WebInventory.rules.recog.json
   Converted from Rapid7 Recog (https://github.com/rapid7/recog), xml/ fingerprint databases,
   commit 1714aaed118861b4567bb6754920b4b929f59380 (v2.3: including snmp_sysdescr, snmp_sysobjid,
   smb_native_os, smb_native_lm and tls_jarm).
   The patterns were translated from Ruby to .NET regex syntax. Rules that .NET could not compile,
   or that failed their own published example, were dropped at conversion time.
   Regenerate: .\Invoke-WebInventory.ps1 -ImportRules .\recog\xml -ImportOutput .\WebInventory.rules.recog.json

   Copyright (c) 2014, Rapid7, Inc.
   All rights reserved.

2. WebInventory.rules.wappalyzer.json
   Converted from enthec/webappanalyzer (https://github.com/enthec/webappanalyzer), a continuation of
   the Wappalyzer technology database, src/technologies/*.json and src/categories.json,
   commit d91f7e510e93457041bea874e8a9ffb011e3e4fe (2026-10-19).
   Modifications: only passive HTTP patterns kept (headers, cookies, meta, scriptSrc, html, scripts,
   text, url, certIssuer, robots); JavaScript regex syntax translated to .NET; field layout changed to
   the WebInventory rule-pack format.

   Licence: GNU General Public License v3.0 - full text in LICENSE-GPL-3.0.txt. The corresponding
   source is the upstream repository at the commit above. Keep LICENSE-GPL-3.0.txt and this notice
   with the pack if you distribute it outside your organisation.
   Regenerate: git clone https://github.com/enthec/webappanalyzer
               .\Invoke-WebInventory.ps1 -ImportRules .\webappanalyzer\src -ImportOutput .\WebInventory.rules.wappalyzer.json

3. Shodan-compatible favicon hash: MurmurHash3 x86_32 (public domain, Austin Appleby),
   re-implemented in C# in the script.

4. JARM active TLS server fingerprinting (-TlsFingerprint, Jarm column)
   Method and packet layout from salesforce/jarm (https://github.com/salesforce/jarm), re-implemented in C#
   in the script; results checked against jarm.py.

   use inside your own organisation that does not directly monetise it is permitted; using it to provide value
   to paying customers (directly or indirectly) needs an OEM licence from FoxIO. FoxIO states that all JA4+

6. NVD CPE names (cpe-supplement table embedded in Invoke-WebInventory.ps1; -ImportRules, -StoreQuery Vulnerabilities)

   The CPE names in the built-in rules and the cpe-supplement table (fill, replace and alias groups, version
   2026.11.06) were checked against the NVD CPE Dictionary 2.0 feed (lastModified 2026-11-04) published by the U.S.
   National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), National Vulnerability Database: https://nvd.nist.gov/

   This product uses data from the NVD API but is not endorsed or certified by the NVD.

   NVD data is a work of the U.S. Government and is not subject to copyright protection in the United States.
   The NVD CVE, KEV and EPSS files given to -StoreQuery Vulnerabilities are downloaded by the operator and are not
   part of this distribution.


7. Version-only rules (v: ids in the built-in pack; src/version-rules.json in the development suite)

   The patterns were written for this tool. Where a product shows its version was established by running the
   product itself, by reading its own page templates, or from public fingerprint collections that record where
   a product prints its version in real responses: WhatWeb passive plugins (https://github.com/urbanadventurer/WhatWeb,
   GPL-2.0), nuclei-templates detection templates (https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates, MIT),
   Rapid7 Recog examples (BSD-2-Clause, see 1) and webappanalyzer patterns (GPL-3.0, see 2). No code, template or
   data file of these projects is included; only the location of a version string was taken from them. Library
   versions are read from the paths of public CDNs (cdnjs, jsDelivr, unpkg); WordPress plugins were installed from
   wordpress.org for testing only.
